newsitem.title: USA: US senators to introduce CFTC reform bill Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: US senators to introduce CFTC reform bill Tuesday.

text.p: U.S. Senators Richard Lugar (R-Ind), Tom Harkin (D-Ia) and Pat Leahy (D-Vt) will introduce a bill Tuesday to update the Commodity Exchange Act to streamline the process of introducing new futures contracts and increase CFTC's authority to police some foreign currency futures.
The legislation would reduce the time required to begin trading new products and reform the process by which exchange rules are reviewed by the CFTC - the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
The bill would also require the CFTC to take costs and benefits into account for many of its activities, with the exception of enforcement.

It also gives CFTC authority to get information from U.S. warehouses that are delivery points for foreign exchanges and directs the CFTC to consult overseas regulators and other appropriate parties in those exchanges' home countries.
The Lugar-Harkin-Leahy bill would amend the so-called "Treasury Amendment" of the 1974 Commodity Exchange Act. That provision excludes some financial products from the CFTC's regulatory coverage.

The new Treasury Amendment language would clarify the CFTC's anthority to police foreign currency futures and options that are traded off-exchange in the United States and are sold to retail investors by entities that are not otherwise federally regulated. Agricultural futures would not be affected.

Lugar, chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee which has authority for the CFTC, said that CFTC reform is a key priority of the committee this session, and that the bill would help the CFTC meet "changing competitive realities."
The Senate Agriculture Committee will hold hearings on the legislation on February 11 and 13.
